LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES: • USE OF DOUBLE IMPERATIVES: • QUESTION TAGS ON THE VERB TO BE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences: • Use of Double Imperatives: • Question Tags on the Verb to be
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences: • Use of Double Imperatives: • Question Tags on the Verb to be, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: What are some of your school rules? 2. How do you give instructions? 3. Why do we ask questions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify tag questions and double imperatives from a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences: • Use of Double Imperatives: • Question Tags on the Verb to be in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences: • Use of Double Imperatives: • Question Tags on the Verb to be in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. advocate the correct use of double imperatives and question tags in communication. Learners is guided to: • Fill in gaps in sentences using double imperatives. • Select question tags from a story, dialogue or poem. • Match statements with the correct question tag to make a tag question. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body/ appropriate Assistive technology with physical support. 1. What are some of your school rules? 2. How do you give instructions? 3. Why do we ask questions? 69 • Practise giving instructions related to the theme using double imperatives such as: shut down your tablets and listen to the teacher. Type this word in your tablet and look up its meaning. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time. • Role play giving and receiving of instructions at home using double imperatives. Learners to be given roles depending on their functional ability. • Use double imperatives to make rules for their classroom and display them in charts or posters. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body or be given physical assistance by peers to display. 70 • Write correct sentences using double imperatives. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body or adapted pens or be assisted by a scribe to write. Core Competency: Self-Efficacy is fostered as the learner formulates school or class rules using double imperatives.
